newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Tirana city hall denies vote list fraud.
newsitem.headline: Tirana city hall denies vote list fraud.

text.p: Tirana city hall on Friday denied allegations by the opposition Socialist Party that it had rigged voting lists in the capital ahead of local elections on October 20, Albanian television reported.
The charges against Tirana city hall, run by the Democratic Party of President Sali Berisha, were made in the Friday edition of Socialist Party newspaper Zeri i Popullit
"The Zeri i Popullit claims and accusations are baseless lies," Tirana city hall said in a statement.

The paper said the Socialists had lodged a complaint with the capital's electoral commission, alleging that the voters' register in Tirana included the names of 22,000 people who had died or left the country.
"If... the lists are not corrected we will start penal cases against those responsible for this electoral falsification," the newspaper quoted Tirana Socialist branch leader Musa Ulqini as saying.
No one at the Socialist Party headquarters was immediately available for comment.

The city hall statement said there were more voters in the capital than in the last elections in 1992 because more districts had been included within the city administrative area and a large number of people had moved to Tirana from the countryside in the past four years.
"Tirana city hall publicly states this is the correct number of voters in Tirana," the statement said.

Albania's nationwide local elections come five months after a disputed general election. Most opposition parties withdrew from that poll, alleging widespread vote manipulation and intimidation -- charges backed by some international observers.

All political parties have put forward heavyweight candidates for the post of Tirana mayor. Western governments have signalled that they consider the local elections a test of Albania's young democracy.
